audit_notes: Slip lengths correct: Philip (1972)/ Lauga & Stone (2003) for L = 20 um, gas fraction 0.9: b_par = (L/pi) ln(sec(pi*0.9/2)) = 6.37 um * ln(6.39) = 11.8 um; b_perp = b_par/2 = 5.9 um. b_par+ = 2.2, b_perp+ = 1.1; net shift 11.8 - 0.6*5.9 = 8.3 um. CRITICAL pressure check: groove gap w = 0.9*20 um = 18 um; with an advancing angle of ~150 deg on the nanotextured ridges the Laplace breakthrough pressure is 2 gamma |cos theta| / w = 2*0.072*0.87/18e-6 = 7.0 kPa = 0.7 m water head. Below ~0.7 m depth the menisci are pushed into the grooves immediately (Cassie-Wenzel), and above it the gas dissolves into undersaturated, turbulent water within hours (mass-transfer coefficient ~3e-4 m/s). On a hull with 10 m draft at most ~5-7% of the wetted area can hold a passive plastron even briefly, and ~0% after days. I therefore adjust plastron_coverage_fraction from 0.7 to 0.05 (optimistic short-term value). Expected gain: 8.3*0.05 = 0.41 um -> 0.4%. The 0.7 value is only reachable with active gas replenishment (see membrane-fed or electrolytic variants). Structural: ridges 2 um wide, 20 um pitch, fine under 50 Pa; nano-texture wears quickly. Baseline: smooth FR (slip 0).
